R1036.summary: Johan Isaac de Swart, Dutch resident at St Petersburg, reports to the Grand Pensionary Pieter van Bleiswijk on the French and Spanish answers to the Austro-Russian mediation proposal, Catherine II's Greek project (Grand Duke Constantine taught Greek and given Greek attendants), and Prussia's accession to the Armed Neutrality.
R1036.en:
High Noble Honourable Sir! I respectfully refer to my humble last letters to Your Honour of the 26th ultimo and the
1st of this month, in which were enclosed the answers of the courts of France and Spain to the proposal which the two
warring courts had sent them following the known preliminary proposal, the courier whom the Austrian minister
received from his court on Sunday, and of which, in mine to the Heer [590] [797] [?made], it is supposed that [29^^]
brought the despatch.

Concerning both the known answers and that of England on the same subject, [228^] just as little as at first both leaves
any means by which the aforesaid warring courts could give their [?mediation] any further effect with [?hope] of
success. The court of England still persisting in some way [...] the American [?colonies] [...] assured that they are
still [?flirting] with the Roman [Emperor] [...].

R1040.summary: De Swart's despatch of 29 November 1787, coded with two codebooks. The 1765-key segment (image 5459 from group 180 to image 5473, 5,625 groups) reports evidence of an Austrian-French alliance, the attention of the Prussian and British representatives at St Petersburg, Kaunitz, the Bavarian exchange and the Duke of Zweibruecken, the German League, the fleet and the Turkish war. The first 1,928 groups and image 5474 (331 groups, 2,259 in all) use a missing Rechteren-family code and are not deciphered.
R1040.en:
All this, [?coupled] with many other circumstances, seems to be indications which make very [?probable] the
[?above-detailed] [917^^] about an effective, if not already [?concluded], at least [?pending] alliance between the
warring court and France. I am also reliably informed that the Prussian minister as well as the English chargé
d'affaires have [?fixed] particular attention on the present dealings here of Austria and France; and as I believe I
understood from the Prussian legation counsellor Hüttel, both ministers [?must] first, just before or at the time of the
above-mentioned courier from Vienna, already have received [265^] from their court, which gave him some notice [695^]
of indications and [?information] which they may have had in Berlin from Vienna [851], that something [...]

system: Three-digit Dutch code-nomenclator (Croiset 1765, Russia legation) with words, syllables and letters; a mark on one digit makes a separate group.
